STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r29.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r29.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r29.claim: The final section again warns against denying God's signs and persisting in idolatry.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r29.anchor: repeats the warnings about denying the signs of God and persisting in idolatry

TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r2.claim: Islam argues against worshipping other gods by showing they are created servants like humans and cannot help, see, or hear as people imagine.
TABATABAI:11:36-49#26/r2.anchor: إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عباد أمثالكم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.claim: People receive every favor from God yet thank others and associate partners incapable of benefiting or harming them.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p137.anchor: while they receive all favours from God, they thank and appreciate others. They associate such partners with God who can neither benefit nor harm them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p155.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p155.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p155.claim: The verse's challenge resembles the challenge in al-Baqarah 2:23.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p155.anchor: The second of the above-cited verses in reality is a challenge similar to the one mentioned in verse 23 of Sūrah al-Baqarah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.claim: The Prophet and Qur’an challenge the Quraysh to summon their supposed deities to rescue them; success would prove the truth of their claims.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.anchor: until then they acknowledged their hypothetical deities the way they wanted to; however, now the Prophet

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.claim: Arab idolaters understood their idols as statues representing angels, jinn, and stars, explaining the address to those called besides God as beings like the worshippers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p156.anchor: the idols worshipped by the Arabs were according to them statues of angels, jinn and stars.

STUDYQURAN:7:194/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r1.claim: The challenge mocks idols and false deities as servants like their worshippers, belonging to God and subject to His sovereignty.
STUDYQURAN:7:194/r1.anchor: mocking these false objects of worship as merely servants like themselves (v. 194), belonging to God and subject to His Sovereignty

TAB-FULL:v10p635/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p635/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p635/r1.claim: Addressing idol worshippers, al-Ṭabarī says the idols they call and worship as gods are servants owned by their Lord, just as humans are His servants; worshipping them is associating partners and disbelief.
TAB-FULL:v10p635/r1.anchor: يقول: هم أملاك لربكم، كما أنتم له مماليك

TAB-FULL:v10p635/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p635/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p635/r2.claim: If idols cannot hear a caller and answer, they cannot harm or benefit; only one who hears requests and can reward, punish, or help can truly bring benefit or harm.

TABATABAI:7:194-195/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r7.claim: The verse argues that the invoked beings are created and governed just as humans are; their failure to answer a summons disproves the knowledge and power implied by worshipping them.
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r7.anchor: إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عباد أمثالكم

TABATABAI:7:194-195/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r9.claim: The passage applies the word servants to inanimate objects.
TABATABAI:7:194-195/r9.anchor: وفي الآيات إطلاق العباد على الجمادات

TABRISI:7:194-195/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r6.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:7:194-195/r6.claim: Al-Hasan says the idols are created beings like their worshippers.

TABRISI:7:194-195/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r7.speaker: الكلبي
TABRISI:7:194-195/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi interprets them as owned beings like their worshippers.

TABRISI:7:194-195/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r8.speaker: الأخفش
TABRISI:7:194-195/r8.claim: Al-Akhfash says they resemble people in being subjected and subdued under God's command; they cannot resist what God wills, so they are servants in the sense of being humbled.
TABRISI:7:194-195/r8.anchor: وقيل: أمثالكم في التسخير أي أنهم مسخرون مذللون لأمر الله عن الأخفش

TABRISI:7:194-195/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:194-195/r9.claim: The root sense of servitude is subduing; the idols' inability to resist God's will makes them servants in the sense of being subdued.
TABRISI:7:194-195/r9.anchor: ولما كانت الأصنام غير ممتنعة مما يريد الله بها كانت في معنى العباد

TABRISI:7:194-195/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:194-195/r10.claim: This second command to invoke them concerns asking the idols for help in urgent needs and for removal of harm.
TABRISI:7:194-195/r10.anchor: هذا الدعاء ليس الدعاء الأول والمراد به فادعوهم في مهماتكم ولكشف الأسواء عنكم

TABRISI:7:194-195/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:194-195/r11.claim: The imperative lām is a challenge meant to expose and ridicule their inability, like the demand “bring your proof if you are truthful.”
TABRISI:7:194-195/r11.anchor: هذه لام الأمر على معنى التعجيز والتهجين كما قال هاتوا برهانكم إن كنتم صادقين

TABRISI:7:194-195/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:194-195/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:7:194-195/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the challenge as “worship them”: will they reward or requite you if you truly expect benefit, reward, intercession, or support?
TABRISI:7:194-195/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس: معناه فاعبدوهم هل يثيبونكم أو يجازونكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r1.claim: The exegetes identify those invoked besides God as idols.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r2.claim: Ata reports from Ibn Abbas that those invoked are angels.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r2.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (يريد: الملائكة)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r3.claim: The angel interpretation is weak: the polytheists of that time worshipped idols, and the next verse describes beings with no walking legs or grasping hands; this points to inanimate idols.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r3.anchor: وهذا القول ضعيف من جهتين أحدهما: إن المشركين في ذلك الوقت كانوا يعبدون الأصنام لا الملائكة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r4.claim: The invocation may mean worship or naming them as gods, and من دون الله means other than God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p528/r4.anchor: ومعنى الدعاء المذكور هاهنا يحتمل أن يكون العبادة، ويحتمل أن يكون التسمية،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r1.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi glosses the idols as owned beings like you.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r2.speaker: الأخفش
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash says they are servants in the sense that they are subdued under God's command; the term for slave likewise reflects subjection.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r3.speaker: قطرب
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r3.claim: Qutrub glosses them as created beings like you.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r4.speaker: أبو بكر بن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbari says the idols are grammatically treated like people because worshippers claim they reason, discern, harm, and benefit; this licenses الذين, masculine plural forms, and عباد, unlike ordinary inanimate objects.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529/r4.anchor: فإن المشركين لما ادعوا أنها تعقل وتميز، وتضر وتنفع أجريت مجرى الناس،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says to worship the idols and ask whether they can reward or repay you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: فاعبدوهم هل يثيبونكم (¬1) أو يجازونكم)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r2.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r2.claim: The people of meaning say the challenge is to seek benefits and removal of harms from the idols, which is impossible; the imperative lām is for incapacitation.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r2.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: (معنى هذا الدعاء: طلب المنافع وكشف المضار من جهتهم،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the condition challenges claims that idols give benefits, reward, intercession, or support.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r3.anchor: إن صدقتم أن لكم عند الأصنام منفعة أو ثوابا أو شفاعة أو نصرة، قاله ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r4.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r4.claim: The صاحب النظم reads إن interrogatively, with an implied hamza: the verse denies that idols are servants like humans, who have reason, hearing, and sight, then challenges their worshippers to summon them; 64:6 and 26:22 exemplify questions without an expressed hamza.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r4.anchor: وسلك صاحب النظم في قوله: {إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عباد أمثالكم} طريقة أخرى؛ فقال: (تأويل قوله: {إن الذين} {إن} على استفهام

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r5.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r5.claim: He argues that this is not a plain assertion: it rhetorically belittles the idols as inferior even to human servants before the following challenge tests their claimed power.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p529#2/r5.anchor: وإنما # قال عز وجل منكرا عليهم أن تكون الأصنام عبادا أمثالهم لقصورها عن أن تكون

QASHANI:7:194/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:194/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:194/r1.claim: Whatever is invoked besides God, human or otherwise, is a servant like the worshippers, equally unable and without independent effect.
QASHANI:7:194/r1.anchor: كائنين من كانوا، ناسا كانوا أو غيرهم

QASHANI:7:194/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:194/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:194/r2.claim: Challenge those invoked to provide what God has not enabled; their failure disproves the attribution of independent efficacy.
QASHANI:7:194/r2.anchor: إلى أمر لا ييسره الله لكم { فليستجيبوا لكم } إلى تيسيره

QASHANI:7:194/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:194/r3.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
QASHANI:7:194/r3.claim: The Prophet tells Ibn Abbas to guard God, ask and seek help only from God, and know that no community can benefit or harm except by what God has written.
QASHANI:7:194/r3.anchor: كما قال النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام لابن عباس: " يا غلام، احفظ الله يحفظك، احفظ الله تجده تجاهك.

QASHANI:7:194/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:194/r4.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
QASHANI:7:194/r4.claim: The same report says all benefit and harm are predetermined, with the pens lifted and pages dried.
QASHANI:7:194/r4.anchor: كما قال النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام لابن عباس: " يا غلام، احفظ الله يحفظك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r2.claim: Those invoked besides God are idols, created and owned beings.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r3.claim: The challenge asks whether idols can reward, requite, or benefit their worshippers, exposing claims that they provide benefit, reward, or intercession.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:193-196/r3.anchor: فاعبدوهم هل يثيبونكم أو يجازونكم!؟ { إن كنتم صادقين } أن لكم عند الأصنام منفعة، أو ثوابا، أو شفاعة

ELMALILI:7:190-198/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:190-198/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:190-198/r9.claim: The idols neither follow a call to guidance nor answer prayers, so seeking their help is futile.
ELMALILI:7:190-198/r9.anchor: Ne arkanızdan yardım ederler ne de dualarınıza

ELMALILI:7:190-198/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:190-198/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:190-198/r10.claim: Elmalılı glosses the worshipped beings as enslaved, senseless, unconscious structures like their worshippers, and cautions that the wording's apparent reference to human slaves is not the intended point.
ELMALILI:7:190-198/r10.anchor: sizin emsâliniz kullardır. Yani sizin gibi akılsız, şuursuz heyâkil-i memlûkedir.

ELMALILI:7:190-198/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:190-198/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:190-198/r11.claim: The intended rebuke is that the polytheists themselves resemble the inert idols they worship.
ELMALILI:7:190-198/r11.anchor: asıl murad bu değil, kendilerinin, taptıkları esnâm ve evsân gibi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r4.claim: Everything worshipped as divine by Arab idolaters or polytheists throughout history is created by God, and there is no deity besides Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r4.anchor: gerek Arap putperestlerinin gerekse tarihin bütün dönemlerindeki müşriklerin tanrısal nitelikler yükleyerek şu veya bu şekilde taptıkları her şey Allah’ın yaratıklarıdır; “O’ndan başka tanrı yoktur.”

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r5.claim: The objects are inanimate, unconscious, and ignorant; they lack divine qualities, cannot guide others, and cannot even hear a call directed to them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r5.anchor: o cansız, şuursuz ve bilgisiz nesneler kendilerine yapılacak çağrıyı bile duyma yeteneğinden yoksundurlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r6.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r6.claim: Shawkani explains that idols, like humans, are servants owned and governed by God and subject to His cosmic laws.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:193/r6.anchor: Allah’ın mülk ve tasarrufunda bulunup O’nun kevnî yasalarına boyun eğerler

BURHAN:v1p118/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p118/r12.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p118/r12.claim: Al-Naḥl says “those they call upon besides God,” while al-Aʿrāf uses “besides Him.”

BURHAN:v4p54/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p54/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p54/r4.claim: Calling the alleged partners God's partners reflects the polytheists' claim, not a divine affirmation of partnership.
BURHAN:v4p54/r4.anchor: وقعت إضافة الشريك إلى الله سبحانه على ما كانوا يقولون

ITQAN:v2p449#4/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p449#4/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p449#4/r1.claim: إن with kasra and no shadda can be a negative particle, entering nominal or verbal clauses; grammarians dispute whether it is restricted to constructions with إلا or لما.
ITQAN:v2p449#4/r1.anchor: أن تكون نافية وتدخل على الاسمية والفعلية

ITQAN:v2p449#4/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p449#4/r5.speaker: الكسائي والمبرد
ITQAN:v2p449#4/r5.claim: Al-Kisaʾi and al-Mubarrad allow negative إن to govern like ليس and apply that parsing to Saʿid ibn Jubayr's reading of this verse.
ITQAN:v2p449#4/r5.anchor: وأجاز الكسائي والمبرد إعمالها عمل ليس وخرج عليه قراءة سعيد ابن جبير

SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r1.claim: The standard reading has إن geminated, with the relative pronoun as its subject and عباد as its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r1.anchor: العامة على تشديد إن فالموصول اسمها وعباد خبرها

SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r2.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads إن lightly with عباد and أمثالكم in the accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r2.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير بتخفيف " إن " ونصب " عباد " و " أمثالكم ". وقد خرجها أبو الفتح ابن جني

SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r3.speaker: أبو الفتح ابن جني
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r3.claim: Ibn Jinnī and others parse the light إن in Saʿīd's reading as a negative particle working like Hijazi ما; this is held by al-Kisāʾī and most Kufans except al-Farrāʾ, and by Basrans Ibn al-Sarrāj, al-Fārisī, and Ibn Jinnī, while reports differ about Sibawayh and al-Mubarrad.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r3.anchor: وقد خرجها أبو الفتح ابن جني وغيره أنها " إن " النافية، وهي عاملة عمل " ما " الحجازية

SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r4.claim: Al-Samīn says the negative particle's accusative government is established in prose and poetry, citing an unattested-by-name poetic line with مستوليا.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r4.anchor: والصحيح أن إعمالها لغة ثابتة نظما ونثرا وأنشدوا:

SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r5.claim: Critics say the negative reading contradicts the canonical affirmation that the idols are servants like people; the answer is that humans can harm and benefit whereas inert idols cannot, so the reading reinforces the canonical meaning a fortiori.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r5.anchor: ولكن قد استشكلوا هذه القراءة من حيث إنها تنفي كونهم عبادا أمثالهم،

SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r6.claim: Abū Jaʿfar rejects the variant for conflicting with the muṣḥaf consonantal form, for Sibawayh's preference to leave light إن ungoverned, and because al-Kisāʾī requires an affirmative after إن.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r6.anchor: وقد رد أبو جعفر هذه القراءة بثلاثة أوجه، أحدها: مخالفتها لسواد المصحف.

SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r7.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r7.claim: The Shaykh answers that Rabiʿa could write accusative nunation without an alif at pause, so the reading need not conflict with the muṣḥaf form; al-Samīn also says the claimed restrictions about Sibawayh and al-Kisāʾī are disputed or unestablished.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r7.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون كتب المنصوب على لغة ربيعة في الوقف على المنون المنصوب بغير ألف

SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r8.claim: Al-Samīn dismisses al-Naḥḥās's objection as slight orthographic variance and says the reports about Sibawayh are disputed and the restriction attributed to al-Kisāʾī is not established.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194/r8.anchor: وما رد به النحاس ليس بشيء لأنها مخالفة يسيرة

SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r1.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r1.claim: The Shaykh parses light إن as operative and cites إن حراسنا أسدا as evidence that it can put both nominal parts in the accusative; he also invokes the reading إن كلا and a poetic example interpreted as ترى رواجعا.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r1.anchor: إن حراسنا أسدا قال: " وهي لغة ثابتة " ثم قال: " فإن تأولنا ما ورد من ذلك نحو:

SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r2.claim: Al-Samīn inventories three parses for the reading: negative إن governing like ما, light operative إن governing both accusatives, or accusatives governed by an implied verb that supplies the predicate's meaning.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r2.anchor: وقد تحصل في تخريج هذه القراءة ثلاثة أوجه: كون " إن " نافية عاملة، أو المخففة الناصبة

SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r3.claim: Al-Samīn notes that the operative-light-إن parse rests on two contested doctrines: applying light إن is rare, and إن and its sisters governing both parts is a weaker grammatical position.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r3.anchor: قلت: فيكون هذا التخريج مبنيا على مذهبين أحدهما: إعمال المخففة وقد نص جماعة من النحويين

SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r4.claim: Some read light إن, accusative عباد, and nominative أمثالكم; they treat إن as ungoverned, الذين as subject, عباد as a circumstantial accusative of its omitted object pronoun, and أمثالكم as predicate, meaning the idols are created and owned like their worshippers.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ بعضهم " إن " مخففة، " عبادا " نصبا، " أمثالكم " رفعا، وتخريجها على أن تكون المخففة

SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r5.claim: Al-Samīn says making the relative pronoun accusative in that last parse is weak because governing with light إن was already described as rare.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r5.anchor: ويضعف أن يكون الموصول اسما منصوب المحل لأن إعمال المخففة كما تقدم قليل

SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r6.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r6.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also transmits a fourth reading, geminated إن with عباد accusative and أمثالكم nominative, parsed like the preceding variant.
SAMIN-DURR:7:194#2/r6.anchor: وحكى أبو البقاء أيضا قراءة رابعة وهي بتشديد " إن " ، ونصب " عباد " ، ورفع " أمثالكم " ، وتخريجها

ASAD-NOTES:7:191#n159/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:191#n159/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:191#n159/r1.claim: Asad reads “servants” as created beings subject to God's will, including living or dead saints and inanimate objects such as idols, fetishes, and physical or mental images of saints or deified persons.
ASAD-NOTES:7:191#n159/r1.anchor: This refers to saints living or dead, as well as to inanimate objects of every description

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f1.claim: The Araf passage describes the worshipped idols as lifeless: they cannot create, help, hear, see, move, or do anything, in contrast with God's hearing and knowledge.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r7#5/f1.anchor: وصف آلهتهم بأنها لا تسمع ولا تبصر ولا تتحرك ولا تقدر على شيء مما يدل على أنها ليس فيها شيء من الحياة

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p269/r5.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p269/r5.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p269/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads عبادا أمثالكم in the accusative; Ibn Jinnī treats إن as a negative particle like ما, though he calls this weak because إن lacks ما’s restricted negation and licensing.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p269/r5.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة سعيد بن جبير: "إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عبادا"2

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p269/r6.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p269/r6.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p269/r6.claim: On Saʿīd’s reading, the idols are stone or wood, less than their rational worshippers; the common nominative reading calls them servants because they too are created, like all created things that glorify God.
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p269/r6.anchor: فكيف يثبت في هذه ما نفاه في هذه؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r1.claim: This sentence confirms the preceding argument that the idols cannot cause benefit or harm.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r1.anchor: هذه الجملة على سبيل التوكيد لما قبلها في انتفاء كون هذه الأصنام قادرة على شيء من نفع أو ضر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r2.claim: The beings called gods are themselves servants of God, who created them and their worshippers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r2.anchor: هم عباد وسمى الأصنام عبادا وإن كانت جمادات لأنهم كانوا يعتقدون فيها أنها تضر وتنفع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r3.speaker: الحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan explains their likeness as being owned by God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r3.anchor: قال الحسن في كونها مملوكة لله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r4.speaker: التبريزي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r4.claim: Al-Tabrīzī explains their likeness as being created.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r5.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r5.claim: Muqātil says this addresses a Khuzāʿa group that worshipped angels; God clarifies that they are servants like their worshippers, not gods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r5.anchor: وقال مقاتل: المراد طائفة من العرب من خزاعة كانت تعبد الملائكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads the comparison as mockery: even if idols were alive and rational, they would still be servants like their worshippers, with no superiority.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: عباد أمثالكم استهزاء بهم أي قصارى أمرهم أن يكونوا أحياء عقلاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī's claim that the following question cancels the likeness: likeness in creation or ownership remains, while the question belittles the idols' missing organs and uses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r7.anchor: وليس كما زعم لأنه تعالى حكم على هؤلاء المدعوين من دون الله أنهم عباد أمثال الداعين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r8.claim: The question about organs cannot invalidate God's earlier statement; that would make one of two divine reports false, which is impossible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r8.anchor: وأيضا فالأبطال لا يتصور بالنسبة إليه تعالى لأنه يدل على كذب أحد الخبرين وذلك مستحيل بالنسبة إلى الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r9.claim: Lacking useful organs does not negate likeness in being created or owned and subdued; the question instead shows idols are inferior to humans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p249/r9.anchor: وإنما ذلك تحقير لشأن الأصنام وأنهم دونكم في انتفاء الآلات التي أعدت للانتفاع بها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r1.speaker: ابن جبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r1.claim: Ibn Jubayr reads a light in and the accusative ʿibādan amthālakum.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r1.anchor: وقرأ ابن جبير إن خفيفة وعبادا أمثالكم بنصب الدال واللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r2.speaker: المفسرون
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r2.claim: Commentators parse this as negative in working like the Ḥijāzī mā: it raises the subject and puts the predicate ʿibādan amthālakum in the accusative, denying likeness to humans.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r2.anchor: واتفق المفسرون على تخريج هذه القراءة على أن إن هي النافية أعملت عمل ما الحجازية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r3.claim: The Kufans, Ibn al-Sarrāj, al-Fārisī, and Ibn Jinnī permit negative in to govern like mā; al-Farrāʾ and most Basrans reject that usage, while reports differ about Sībawayh and al-Mubarrad.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r3.anchor: وإعمال إن إعمال ما الحجازية فيه خلاف أجاز ذلك الكسائي وأكثر الكوفيين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r4.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the correct position is that in can work like mā; this is a usage attested in both prose and poetry.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r4.anchor: والصحيح أن إعمالها لغة ثبت ذلك في النثر والنظم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r5.claim: He rejects the negative-in parsing because it denies likeness, contradicting the majority reading that affirms it and implying incompatible divine reports.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r5.anchor: والذي يظهر لي أن هذا التخريج الذي خرجوه من أن إن للنفي ليس بصحيح لأن قراءة الجمهور تدل على إثبات كون الأصنام عبادا أمثال عابديها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r6.speaker: النحاس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r6.claim: Al-Naḥḥās objects to the reading because it differs from the codex consonantal text, conflicts with Sībawayh's preferred nominative predicate, and conflicts with al-Kisāʾī's account of negative in.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r6.anchor: وقال النحاس: هذه قراءة لا ينبغي أن يقرأ بها لثلاث جهات إحداها أنها مخالفة للسواد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r7.claim: Abū Ḥayyān answers that the reading is transmitted from a distinguished Successor, its orthographic difference is slight and perhaps reflects Rabīʿa spelling, and the accounts of Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī are disputed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p250/r7.anchor: وكلام النحاس هذا هو الذي لا ينبغي لأنها قراءة مروية عن تابعي جليل ولها وجه في العربية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r1.claim: Another parsing takes lightened in as still emphatic and governing like full inna, allowing ʿibādan as its accusative predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r1.anchor: المضمر بالقراءة المتواترة وإن كلا لما وبنقل سيبويه عن العرب لكنه نصب في هذه القراءة خبرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r2.speaker: عمر بن أبي ربيعة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r2.claim: A line by ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa supplies an example of an accusative predicate after inna.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r3.speaker: جماعة من النحاة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r3.claim: Some grammarians allow accusative predicates with inna and its sisters, citing clear poetic evidence; their opponents interpret those examples differently.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r3.anchor: وقد ذهب جماعة من النحاة إلى جواز نصب أخبار إن وأخواتها واستدلوا على ذلك بشواهد ظاهرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r4.claim: Alternatively, opponents can treat the accusative as an omitted verb, as in the poem about wishing youth's days back; this keeps both readings equivalent in meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r4.anchor: وهو أنهم تأولوا المنصوب على إضمار فعل كما قالوا في قوله: يا ليت أيام الصبا رواجعا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r5.claim: Another reading lightens in and puts ʿibādan in the accusative as a circumstantial accusative from an omitted pronoun in the relative clause; amthālakum is nominative predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r5.anchor: وقرىء أيضا إن مخففة ونصب عبادا على أنه حال من الضمير المحذوف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r6.claim: Whether the likeness is in creation or ownership, such beings cannot be gods.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r6.anchor: أي إن الذين تدعونهم من دون الله في حال كونهم عبادا أمثالكم في الخلق أو في الملك فلا يمكن أن يكونوا آلهة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r7.claim: The imperative to call them is a challenge: test by invoking them whether they can answer; they cannot.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r7.anchor: فادعوهم أي فاختبروهم بدعائكم هل يقع منهم إجابة أو لا يقع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r8.claim: The challenge is like the statement that if they heard the call, they would not respond.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r8.anchor: والأمر بالاستجابة هو على سبيل التعجيز أي لا يمكن أن يجيبوا كما قال: ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r9.claim: Being truthful means that the idolaters' claim that their gods are divine and deserve worship is true.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r9.anchor: ومعنى إن كنتم صادقين في دعوى إلهيتهم واستحقاق عبادتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r10.claim: Abū Ḥayyān compares the challenge to Abraham's question to his father about worshipping what cannot hear, see, or help.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p251/r10.anchor: كقول إبراهيم عليه السلام لأبيه لم تعبد ما لا يسمع ولا يبصر ولا يغني عنك شيئا

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r1.claim: The verse confirms the preceding point that the idols do not follow their worshippers’ calls.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r1.anchor: تقرير لما قبله من عدم إتباعهم لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r2.claim: “Calling” may mean worship, naming the idols as gods, or invoking them; in the worship and naming readings, the two objects are omitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r2.anchor: والدعاء إما بمعنى العبادة تسمية لها بجزئها أو بمعنى التسمية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r3.claim: The omitted objects mean either that they worship the idols besides God or that they name them gods besides Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r3.anchor: أو تسمونهم آلهة من دونه سبحانه وتعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r4.claim: The idols, like their worshippers, are owned by God, subject to His command, and incapable of benefit or harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r4.anchor: مملوكة لله تعالى مسخرة لأمره عاجزة عن النفع والضر

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r5.claim: Though the idols are even more visibly powerless, likening them to their worshippers confronts people who admit their own weakness yet claim idols can act.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r5.anchor: مع كون عجزها عنهما أظهر وأقوى من عجزهم إنما هو لاعترافهم بعجز أنفسهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r6.claim: A further possibility is that carved human-shaped idols are treated hypothetically as living, rational beings like their makers, yet still unworthy of worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r6.anchor: لما نحتوا الأصنام بصور الأناسي قال سبحانه لهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r7.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads inna with a light n and ʿibādan in the accusative.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r7.anchor: قرأ سعيد بن جبير ( إن الذين تدعون ) بتخفيف إن ونصب عبادا أمثالكم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r8.speaker: ابن جني
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r8.claim: Ibn Jinnī parses the light form as a negative إن functioning like the Hijazi mā, an analysis associated with al-Kisāʾī and some Kufans.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r8.anchor: وخرجها ابن جني على أن إن نافية عملت عمل ما الحجازية وهو مذهب الكسائي وبعض الكوفيين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r9.claim: Critics object that this negative construction is unattested and appears to deny the likeness asserted by the familiar reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r9.anchor: واعترض أولا بأنه لم يثبت مثل ذلك وثانيا بأنه يقتضي نفي كونهم عبادا أمثالهم

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r10.claim: The replies say the construction occurs in Arabic; the readings need not conflict because one can affirm likeness in one respect while the other denies it wholly or in another respect.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r10.anchor: وعن الثاني أنه لا تناقض لأن المشهورة تثبت المثلية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r11.claim: Another parsing treats the light إن as a weakened heavy إن that unusually governs both accusatives; because this is rare and weak, some leave إن ungoverned and supply an omitted predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r11.anchor: إنها إن المخففة من المثقلة وإنها على لغة من نصب بها الجزئين

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r12.claim: A recited heavy anna has ʿibādan as a circumstantial accusative from the omitted pronoun and amthālukum as its nominative predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r12.anchor: بالتشديد و ( عبادا ) بالنصب على أنه حال من العائد المحذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r13.claim: A further transmitted form has amthālukum nominative with the light reading and ʿibād accusative, parsed as a circumstantial accusative plus predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r13.anchor: في قراءة التخفيف ونصب ( عباد ) وخرج ذلك على الحالية والخبرية

ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r14.claim: The command is a taunting challenge: call on the idols to remove harm or bring benefit if the worshippers are truthful.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p143#4/r14.anchor: تحقيق لمضمون ما قبله بتعجيزهم وتبكيتهم أي فادعوهم في رفع ضرأ وجلب نفع

ALUSI-FULL:v9p144/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144/r1.claim: The challenge concerns the worshippers’ claim that their idols can do what the worshippers themselves cannot.
ALUSI-FULL:v9p144/r1.anchor: قادرون على ما أنتم عاجزون عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r22.claim: In this reading, whatever is invoked besides God shares human incapacity and has no independent effect.

ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v9p155#2/r23.claim: The challenge asks the worshippers to call their alleged partners about any matter and test whether they truly attribute efficacy to them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r1.claim: Those invoked besides God are the idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r1.anchor: {إن الذين تدعون من دون الله} يعني الأصنام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r2.claim: Calling them servants like you means they are owned as you are; alternatively, they are subjected to whatever is done with them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r2.anchor: {عباد أمثالكم} يريد أنها مملوكة أمثالكم. وقيل: أمثالكم في التسخير، أي: أنهم مسخرون مذللون لما أريد منهم.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r3.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r3.claim: Muqatil says the phrase refers to angels, addressing people who worshipped angels; the author says the first interpretation is sounder.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: قوله "عباد أمثالكم" أراد به الملائكة، والخطاب مع قوم كانوا يعبدون الملائكة. والأول أصح.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r4.claim: The challenge means invoke them to answer if you are truthful that they are gods.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r4.anchor: {فادعوهم فليستجيبوا لكم إن كنتم صادقين} أنها آلهة،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses invoke them as worship them: will they reward or save you if you truly expect benefit from them?
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p315/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: فاعبدوهم، هل يثيبونكم أو يجاوزونكم إن كنتم صادقين أن لكم عندها منفعة؟

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r1.claim: Calling them means worshipping them and naming them gods.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r1.anchor: تدعون من دون الله } أي تعبدونهم وتسمونهم آلهة

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r2.claim: The idols are servants like humans in being owned and subjected.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r3.claim: If the idols really are gods, call them and see whether they can answer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r3.anchor: فادعوهم فليستجيبوا لكم إن كنتم صدقين

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r4.claim: Alternatively, carved in human form, their utmost status would be living rational beings like their worshippers, who are no more entitled to worship one another.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:194/r4.anchor: لما نحتوها بصور الأناسي قال لهم: إن قصارى أمرهم

BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r1.claim: The invocation is bound to worship: the polytheists invoke their idols as objects of worship, and calling is inseparable from the one worshipped.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r1.anchor: أي أيها المشركون كون دعاء عبادة ملازمين لذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r2.claim: Alternatively, invocation is used for worship to show that one incapable of being invoked cannot rightly be worshipped.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r2.anchor: أو أنه أطلق الدعاء على العبادة إشارة إلى أنه لا تصح عبادة من ليس فيه قابيلة أن يدعى

BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r3.claim: The idols are powerless servants like their worshippers, especially unable to meet the Qur’an’s challenge; humans surpass them in life and reason, while a true deity cannot be like a worshipper.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r3.anchor: أي في العجز عن كل شيء لا سيما عما وقع بع التحدي من معارضة القرآن وغيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r4.claim: The challenge is to call them to anything and see if they answer clearly, produce a comparable surah, or provide any benefit; a true god would answer a devotee.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r4.anchor: ولما كان الإله الحق يجيب وليه عند التحدي من غير تخلف

BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads إن lightly and عبادا أمثالكم with the accusative, treating إن as a negative particle that raises its noun and sets its predicate in the accusative.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r5.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير { إن } خفيفة و { عبادا أمثالكم بنصب الدال واللام

BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r6.claim: Grammarians dispute whether إن may work like الحجازية ما: al-Kisāʾī, most Kufans, Ibn al-Sarrāj, al-Fārisī, and Ibn Jinnī allow it; al-Farrāʾ and most Basrans reject it, with reports differing on Sibawayh and al-Mubarrad.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r6.anchor: وإعمالها هذا العمل فيه خلاف , أجازه الكسائي وأكثر الكوفيين , ومن البصريين ابن السراج والفارسي وابن جني

BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r7.claim: Biqāʿī holds that this grammatical use of إن is a documented language found in both verse and prose.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r7.anchor: والصيحح أن إعمالها لغة ثبت ذلك في النظم والنثر

BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r8.claim: The negative reading need not conflict with the familiar affirmative: affirmation concerns shared incapacity, while denial concerns equality, since people exceed idols in other capacities.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r8.anchor: وليس الأمر هنا كذلك , فالاثبات لمماثلتها لهم في مطلق العجز

BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī resolves the readings by taking the affirmative as concessive and the negation as the literal truth.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p170/r9.anchor: قال الزمخشري - أن الإثبات على سبيل التنزل والنفي على الحقيقة

DURR-FULL:v3p626/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p626/r8.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v3p626/r8.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr reports that the sun and moon will be brought before God along with those who worshipped them, and they will be told to call on them if they are truthful.
DURR-FULL:v3p626/r8.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: يجاء بالشمس والقمر حتى يلقيان بين يدي الله ويجاء بمن كان يعبدهما فيقال {فادعوهم فليستجيبوا لكم إن كنتم صادقين}

IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636/r1.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636/r1.claim: On the Resurrection, the sun and moon and their worshipers will be brought before God, and the worshipers will be told to call upon them.
IBNABIHATIM:v5p1636/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال : يجاء بالشمس والقمر يوم القيامة حتى يلقيان بين يدي الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r1.claim: On the first reading of the preceding address, this begins a new address to the polytheists; emphasis counters their denial that idols share their servitude, and the wording shifts from third person to direct address.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r1.anchor: ولذلك صدر بحرف التوكيد لأن المشركين ينكرون مساواة الأصنام إياهم في العبودية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r2.claim: The relative phrase refers to idols and alerts the polytheists that their invocation is misguided; ʿAbda ibn al-Ṭabīb’s similar relative phrasing is cited as a parallel.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r2.anchor: فهذا الموصول كالموصول في قول عبدة بن الطبيب : إن الذين ترونهم إخوانكم يشفي غليل صدورهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r3.claim: If the prior address was to the Prophet and Muslims, this sentence independently turns to address the polytheists.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r3.anchor: أن تكون استئنافا ابتدائيا انتقل به إلى مخاطبة المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r4.claim: On the alternative reading of the preceding address, this sentence explains why the idols do not follow guidance: they are servants, hence created beings.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r4.anchor: أن تكون هذه الجملة بيانا وتعليلا لجملة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r5.claim: ʿAbd originally means a person owned rather than free, then Arabic extended it to any creature, as in the cited Qurʾanic uses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r5.anchor: أصله المملوك ، ضد الحر ، كما في قوله تعالى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r6.claim: Although ʿabd commonly denotes human creatures, Arabs used rational plural forms for idols, so the plural address follows prevalent usage of the period.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r6.anchor: والمشهور أنه لا يطلق إلا على المخلوقات من الآدميين فيكون إطلاق العباد على الأصنام كإطلاق ضمير جمع العقلاء عليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r7.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r7.claim: Al-Kashshāf treats calling idols servants as mockery of the polytheists: even if idols were alive and rational, they would still be creatures like their worshippers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r7.anchor: وجعله صاحب ( الكشاف ) اطلاق تهكم واستهزاء بالمشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r8.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers a metaphorical usage by assumed concord: since worshippers and idols are alike as created beings, he calls their counterparts servants as worshippers are servants of God.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p220/r8.anchor: والأحسن عندي أن يكون إطلاق العباد عليهم مجازا بعلاقة الإطلاق عن التقييد روعي في حسنة المشاكلة التقديرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r1.claim: The command to call the idols is a challenge: invocation is possible but their response is not, exposing both their impotence and the worshippers’ inability to establish their claim; 35:14 makes the same point.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r1.anchor: لأن نفس الدعاء ممكن ولكن استجابته لهم ليست ممكنة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r2.claim: The intended call is most likely a plea for aid and victory; al-Māzinī’s verse says those summoned to rescue do not ask what war or place is involved.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r2.anchor: والأظهر أن المراد بالدعوة المأمور بها الدعوة للنصر والنجدة كما قال وذاك المازني إذا استنجدوا لم يسألوا من دعاهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r3.claim: The challenge is a metonymy for the idols’ inability to answer and the polytheists’ inability to display an invocation followed by a response.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r3.anchor: وبهذا يظهر أن أمر التعجيز كناية عن ثبوت عجز الأصنام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r4.claim: The lām makes this a third-person imperative challenging the idols; the ordinary form of a command addressed to an absent party is an imperative with lām.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r4.anchor: أمر تعجيز للأصنام ، وهو أمر الغائب فإن طريق أمر الغائب هو الأمر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r5.claim: Addressing the absent idols through the hearers entails that the hearers must deliver the command; the idols’ inability to receive that message itself signals their inability to respond.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v9p221/r5.anchor: ومعنى توجيه أمر الغائب السامع أنه مأمور بأن يبلغ الأمر للغائب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r1.speaker: جمهور الناس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r1.claim: The majority read inna with a geminated nūn and ʿibād in the nominative; the address belittles idols as created, material bodies that are themselves subject to worship or ownership.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r1.anchor: قرأ جمهور الناس «إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عباد أمثالكم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r2.claim: Maqātil says the verse addresses a group of Khuzaʿa who worshipped angels, informing them that angels are servants like them, not gods.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل، إن المراد بهذه الآية طائفة من العرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r3.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr reads the nūn of in lightly and puts ʿibādan and amthālakum in the accusative: in means “not,” denying that idols are servants like humans.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير «إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عبادا أمثالكم»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r4.claim: On Saʿīd b. Jubayr’s reading, the idols are less and baser than humans because they are inert and cannot understand or reason.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r4.anchor: بل هم أقل وأحقر إذ هي جمادات لا تفهم ولا تعقل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r5.claim: Sībawayhi says in meaning mā is too weak to govern the predicate, so it remains nominative; this is the grammatical form he considers correct for the reading.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r5.anchor: وسيبويه يرى أن «إن» إذا كانت بمعنى «ما» فإنها تضعف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r6.speaker: أبو العباس المبرد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r6.claim: Al-Mubarrad permits in when it means mā to govern like mā and put its predicate in the accusative.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r6.anchor: وأبو العباس المبرد يجيز أن تعمل عمل «ما» في نصب الخبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r7.speaker: الكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r7.claim: Al-Kisāʾī says in meaning mā only occurs with illā, as in 67:2.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r7.anchor: وزعم الكسائي أن «إن» بمعنى «ما» لا تجيء إلا وبعدها إلا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r8.claim: The command is a test: call the idols, and if they do not answer, that confirms the description just given.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p488#2/r8.anchor: ثم بين تعالى الحجة بقوله فادعوهم أي فاختبروا فإن لم يستجيبوا فهم كما وصفنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r1.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr’s reading, understood as negation, entails that idols are not servants like human beings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p489/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: و «تتقون» بهذا التأويل قراءة سعيد بن جبير

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r1.claim: Those invoked apart from God are idols.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r1.anchor: يعني الأصنام ﴿ عباد أمثالكم ﴾ في أنهم مسخرون مذللون لأمر الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r2.claim: The idols are called servants like people because they too are subjected and humbled to God's command.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r2.anchor: في أنهم مسخرون مذللون لأمر الله وإنما قال عباد وقال

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r3.claim: The challenge says to call on them despite their being inanimate, as explained under the earlier phrase that they are created.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r3.anchor: لما بينا عند قوله ﴿ وهم يخلقون ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r4.claim: The phrase means let them answer you.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r4.anchor: أي فليجيبوكم ﴿ إن كنتم صادقين ﴾ أن لكن عندهم نفعا وثوابا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p306/r5.claim: The challenge asks whether the idols can provide benefit or reward.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p529#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p529#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p529#2/r3.claim: The idols are creatures like their worshippers; humans are more complete because they hear, see, and act, while idols do none of these things.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p529#2/r3.anchor: ثم ذكر تعالى أنها عبيد مثل عابديها، أي: مخلوقات مثلهم، بل الأناسي أكمل منها،

JISHUMI:v4p2813/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r15.claim: Duʿāʾ is a request for an action in a specified verbal form, which may be an imperative, a prohibition, or a statement such as ‘May God forgive him.’
JISHUMI:v4p2813/r15.anchor: الدعاء: طلب الفعل بصيغة مخصوصة، ثم تختلف صيغته فيكون بصيغة الأمر والنهي والإخبار،

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r1.claim: تدعون means worshipping them and naming them gods besides God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r1.anchor: أي تعبدونهم وتسمونهم آلهة من دون الله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r2.claim: The phrase mocks the idols: even if they were living and rational, they would merely be servants like their worshippers, with no superiority; the next questions deny they can act like people.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r2.anchor: استهزاء بهم ، أي قصارى أمرهم أن يكونوا أحياء عقلاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r3.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r3.claim: Another interpretation takes عباد أمثالكم to mean that the idols are owned or subjected, as you are.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r4.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr reads إن lightly and عبادا in the accusative: ‘Those you invoke are not servants like you’; إن works like the negative ما of Hijazi Arabic.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p178/r4.anchor: سعيد بن جبير : ( إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عبادا أمثالكم )

MUQATIL:7:190-197/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:190-197/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:190-197/r9.claim: Those worshipped besides God are idols, servants like their worshippers, and not gods.
MUQATIL:7:190-197/r9.anchor: يعنى تعبدون { من دون الله } من الآلهة، إنهم { عباد أمثالكم } ، وليسوا بآلهة

MUQATIL:7:190-197/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:190-197/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:190-197/r10.claim: The challenge is to ask the idols to respond by proving they are gods if their worshippers are truthful.
MUQATIL:7:190-197/r10.anchor: { فادعوهم } ، يعنى فاسألوهم، { فليستجيبوا لكم } بأنهم آلهة، { إن كنتم صادقين }

NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#4/r1.claim: «Those you call» means those you worship and name as gods.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#4/r2.claim: The idols are servants like their worshippers: created, owned, and controlled.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#4/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#4/r3.claim: Call on them to bring benefit or avert harm; let them answer if you truly believe they are gods.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p51#4/r3.anchor: ﴾ لجلب نفع أو دفع ضر ﴿ فليستجيبوا لكم ﴾ فليجيبوا

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r1.claim: Here tadʿūna means that the polytheists worship the idols.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r2.claim: An alternative takes it to mean that they call the idols gods.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r3.claim: Min dūni Allāh means other than God.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r3.anchor: «من دون الله» أي من غير الله

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r4.claim: The idols are called servants because they are owned by God and subjected to Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r4.anchor: وسميت الأوثان عبادا لأنها مملوكة لله مسخرة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r5.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the idols are created beings like you.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r5.anchor: الحسن: المعنى أن الأصنام مخلوقة أمثالكم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r6.claim: The masculine wording treats idols as people because polytheists thought they could harm and benefit like people.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r6.anchor: ولما اعتقد المشركون أن الأصنام تضر وتنفع أجراها مجرى الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r7.claim: The challenge is to ask the idols for benefit or harm.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r7.anchor: ومعنى «فادعوهم» أي فاطلبوا منهم النفع والضر

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r8.claim: The challenge tests their claim that worshipping idols brings benefit.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the command means worship them.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: معنى فادعوهم فاعبدوهم

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r11.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r11.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr reads inna lightly with kasra and reads ʿibādan and amthālakum in the accusative.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r11.anchor: قرأ سعيد بن جبير: «إن الذين تدعون من دون الله عبادا أمثالكم»

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r12.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r12.claim: On Saʿīd ibn Jubayr’s reading, idols are stone and wood, so people worship what is nobler than themselves.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r12.anchor: أي هي حجارة وخشب فأنتم تعبدون ما أنتم أشرف منه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r13.speaker: النحاس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r13.claim: Al-Naḥḥās rejects this reading: it conflicts with the codex; Sibawayh favors a nominative predicate after inna used as mā; al-Kisāʾī says inna rarely means mā without an affirmative.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r13.anchor: قال النحاس: وهذه قراءة لا ينبغي أن يقرأ بها من ثلاث جهات

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r14.claim: The lām in fal-yastajībū is originally kasra, omitted because it is heavy.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r14.anchor: الأصل أن تكون اللام مكسورة، فحذفت الكسرة لثقلها

QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r15.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r15.claim: An ellipsis means: invite them to follow you and let them respond if you are right that they are gods.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:194-196/r15.anchor: في الكلام حذف، المعنى: فادعوهم إلى أن يتبعوكم

BURSEVI:v3p226/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p226/r1.claim: The objects worshipped besides God are idols called gods, yet are owned, governed, and unable to bring benefit or harm.
BURSEVI:v3p226/r1.anchor: أي : تعبدونهم من دونه تعالى من الأصنام وتسمونهم آلهة

BURSEVI:v3p226/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226/r2.speaker: الحدادي
BURSEVI:v3p226/r2.claim: Al-Haddadi says the idols are called servants because their makers fashioned them in human form.
BURSEVI:v3p226/r2.anchor: وقال الحدادي : سماها عبادا لأنهم صوروها على صورة الإنسان

BURSEVI:v3p226/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p226/r3.claim: The challenge is to call the idols for benefit or removal of harm; the command that they respond is a taunt meant to show their incapacity.

BURSEVI:v3p226/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p226/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p226/r4.claim: Their claim is that the idols can do what their worshippers cannot; the challenge exposes that claim as false.
BURSEVI:v3p226/r4.anchor: في زعمكم أنهم قادرون على ما أنتم عاجزون عنه

RAZI-FULL:v15p74/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p74/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p74/r7.claim: Calling idols servants like worshippers raises the question how this applies to inanimate objects; al-Razi begins by answering that the wording addresses idolaters' beliefs.
RAZI-FULL:v15p74/r7.anchor: وفيه سؤال : وهو أنه كيف يحسن وصفها بأنها عباد مع أنها جمادات ؟ وجوابه من وجوه : الأول

RAZI-FULL:v15p74/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p74/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p74/r8.claim: Because idolaters claim idols benefit and harm, the verse addresses them as if they believe idols intelligent; masculine الذين and فليستجيبوا match that presumed belief.
RAZI-FULL:v15p74/r8.anchor: ادعوا أنها تضر وتنفع ، وجب أن يعتقدوا فيها كونها عاقلة فاهمة

RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r1.claim: Rāzī reads the concession sarcastically: even if idols were living and rational, they would be fellow servants, so humans have no basis for making them gods; the next verse refutes even this concession.
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r1.anchor: فإن ثبت ذلك فهم عباد أمثالكم ولا فضل لهم عليكم

RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r2.claim: Calling the idols means asking them to bring benefits or remove harms; the imperative lām in “let them respond” is a challenge showing their incapacity and unsuitability for worship.
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r2.anchor: ومعنى هذا الدعاء طلب المنافع وكشف المضار من جهتهم

RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r3.claim: The condition challenges the idolaters to prove their claim that the idols are gods deserving worship.
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r3.anchor: أي في ادعاء أنها آلهة ومستحقة للعبادة

RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r4.claim: Rāzī compares the argument with Abraham’s rebuke to his father for worshipping what cannot hear, see, or benefit him.
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r4.anchor: ونظيره قول إبراهيم عليه السلام لأبيه

RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r5.claim: Since three conclusive proofs show idols are unfit for worship, a rational person should turn only to the God who is powerful, knowing, living, wise, and able to harm and benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v15p75/r5.anchor: ولما ثبت بهذه الدلائل الثلاثة اليقينية أنها لا تصلح للمعبودية
